proposal:
SCOPE. Hand-derived; nothing executed. One unimplemented root-only extension, FSL (fiber-slack lifting), continuing RCQ. It is tractable-family detection with a quantitative boundary, not a general SAT algorithm. No universal growth bound is claimed.

OBJECT. Fix a subspace K of F_2^n with quotient map pi and r = n - dim K. For a block B (support S, forbidden set P_B) let K_S be the projection of K to S and rho_B = dim K_S. Split P_B into full K_S-cosets (the RCQ core) and the residual E_B (points in partially forbidden cosets). The core defines G as today: G(y)=0 iff some block's coset at y is fully forbidden. New invariant, the fiber mass: mu(y) = sum over blocks whose coset c_B(y) is only partially forbidden of |P_B ∩ c_B(y)| / 2^rho_B. Its y-free bound is M* = sum_B max over partial cosets c of |P_B ∩ c| / 2^rho_B. M* is computable from the clause list without enumerating 2^n or 2^r points.

CLAIM T14a (proof sketch only). Restriction from a fiber x0+K to S is affine onto x0|_S+K_S with uniform preimage size, so block B kills exactly the fraction |P_B ∩ c_B(y)| / 2^rho_B of fiber y. Hence G(y)=1 and mu(y)<1 imply fiber y contains a model of F. If M*<1 then SAT(F) iff SAT(G), and any G-model lifts by conditional expectations over a basis of K (each conditional count is a rank computation).

OUTCOMES. (i) G UNSAT gives F UNSAT (this is RCQ). (ii) A G-model y with mu(y)<1 gives SAT with an explicit x. (iii) Otherwise UNKNOWN: skip, original solver and order intact.

SOUNDNESS ACCOUNTING. No answer depends on T14a. SAT answers are checked by evaluating F at the lifted x. UNSAT answers use the already Lean-proved complete-enumeration rule on the core sub-formula plus the trivial fact that F implies its core. T14a is only a completeness and total-work statement: under M*<1 one G-model suffices, with no backtracking over base models.

WORK. Given K, coset bucketing, rho_B, M* and the lift are polynomial in encoded length L (Gaussian elimination per block and per lift step; dyadic rationals of at most n+log m bits). Two costs stay unbounded: solving G, and the deployed 2^n core check. Discovery is heuristic with no completeness claim. Per block, histogram the pairwise differences p+q of forbidden points (at most m^2 vector XORs in total), keep differences with count > 2|P_B|/3 as near-periods, span them, and set K-perp to the sum of the block annihilators. Then recompute saturation. If |E_B| < |P_B|/3 every true period passes. Spurious periods only enlarge K_S and raise M*, which causes refusal, never unsoundness.

FAILURE VS HARDNESS. Neon auto00037 skips because two singleton blocks cover all variables. Hand analysis: K-perp = span{x1+x5+x6, x2+x7+x8, x3+x9+x10, x4+x11+x12}; core = clauses 1-96; G = {y1|y2, -y2|y3, y1|-y3, -y1|y4, y2|-y4, -y3|-y4}, which is UNSAT. Both long clauses have rho=6, so M* = 2/64 = 1/32. I classify its peak 16 as compression failure, not a harder trace. Test: the deployed solver on clauses 1-96 alone, compression disabled, same order, should also peak 16.

For auto00008 I make no solving claim; its formula is not in this brief. Diagnostic: compute r = dim of the sum of Ann(Stab_B). If r<11, an exact linear quotient exists and the skip is a greedy-basis artifact. If r=11, no exact translation quotient exists and peak 16 is a genuine trace for this solver family.

INDEPENDENT TESTS (fixture null because FSL is not deployed).
P1: FSL on auto00037 returns UNSAT at root with M*=1/32 and zero DP states.
P2: delete clauses 81-96 (block {3,4,9,10,11,12}). G becomes satisfiable, only by y=(1,1,1,1). FSL returns SAT; the true-set {1,5,6,7,9,11} is a valid lift. Brute force must agree.
P3 (sharpness): append [5,7],[5,-7],[-5,9],[-5,-9] to P2 with K held fixed. F is UNSAT, G is SAT, mass = 1/2+1/2+1/32. FSL must return UNKNOWN, not SAT.
P4: random base 2-CNFs on r<=6 XOR forms plus residual clauses with M*<1. FSL must equal brute force on every instance; one disagreement refutes T14a or the implementation.
missing_theorem:
T14.
(a) Routine Lean target (finite counting over F_2): the fiber-mass lemma. For K <= F_2^n, block (S,P) and fiber x0+K: #{x in x0+K : x|_S in P} = |P ∩ (x0|_S+K_S)| * 2^(dim K - rho). Corollary: G(y)=1 and mu(y)<1 imply there is x with pi(x)=y and F(x), found by a conditional-expectation lift in poly(L) bit operations. Tightness: with K=F_2^2 and F={(a),(-a|b),(-a|-b)}, no coset is saturated, M*=1, G is identically true and F is UNSAT. So '<1' cannot be relaxed in the union-bound form.
(b) FIRST GENUINELY MISSING (conjecture): planted recovery. Suppose F = core AND residual for a planted K with M*<1, and every block has |E_B|<|P_B|/3. Add a separation hypothesis H, conjecturally: no non-period t has autocorrelation |Q_B ∩ (Q_B+t)| > 2|P_B|/3 on the saturated part Q_B. Then the difference-histogram procedure outputs K' with M*(K')<1 in O(m^2 n + m n^3) bit operations. Without H the statement is false (see self_attack). The missing step is an H that is checkable from the input rather than assumed.
(c) Open, not attempted: any total-work bound when M*>=1. With K=F_2^n every CNF is its own residual, so that regime is unrestricted SAT. Work(G) is never bounded by FSL.
self_attack:
1. This is another certified tractable family. Its boundary M*<1 is exact for the union bound, but nothing here approaches general polynomial SAT.
2. On UNSAT instances FSL adds nothing beyond RCQ; P1 is an RCQ outcome. The increment is the SAT side and the no-backtracking statement. The deployed solver's early SAT exit may already handle P2, so the measured gain could be zero.
3. It is not robust to extra clauses in the strong sense. In the 36-clause extra-point control, if blocks are 4-point cosets on 4-variable supports (inferred from counts, not seen), each added point has fraction 1/4, so M* reaches 9/4 and FSL refuses via M*. The deployed solver already peaks 0 there. The fiber residual is a 2-CNF in kernel coordinates that depends on y, so I claim no recursion.
4. Punctured cosets defeat it. Deleting one point from a forbidden coset leaves fraction 1-2^-rho; two such blocks give mass >=1. So one-point-perturbed XOR gadgets of the auto00009 type are handled only when the perturbation adds points, not when it removes them.
5. Discovery adversary: extra clauses forming a coset of a wrong subgroup, or a base with large near-stabilizers, pass the 2/3 threshold. The span grows, everything becomes residual, and FSL refuses. The threshold is arbitrary and near-periods are not a subgroup (two 2/3-periods only guarantee a 1/3-period).
6. Writing G as plain CNF still needs an adapted basis or redundant frame variables, which may exceed n. Incompatible greedy bases, and so auto00008, remain unsolved.
7. 'Polynomial' refers to the certificate arithmetic given K, not to the solver. The bounded deployment would still enumerate 2^n for the core.
8. My decoding of auto00037 is by hand. A sign error would falsify P1-P3, which is their purpose.
mechanism_signature: FSL | unimplemented | root-only | two-sided extension of the RCQ core | invariant: fiber mass mu(y)=sum |P ∩ coset|/2^rho, bound M* | accept SAT iff a G-model has mu<1 (uniform if M*<1), UNSAT iff G UNSAT, else skip | SAT self-certified by lifted x, UNSAT by existing core certificate | discovery: pairwise-difference histogram, 2/3 threshold, heuristic | refuses at mass >=1
